new.headline: A 3:50 marathon with a 12-minute PR is a real result, so this week is for walking, sleeping and letting the quads come back. Tell me what you want next and we will shape the weeks ahead.

answers.question: How long before I can run again? A friend wants me to race the Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks.
answers.answer:
Give it a full week with no running. Walking is good, stairs and easy movement are good, and the quads will tell you when they are ready. Most runners start short, slow jogs 7 to 10 days after a marathon, then build back over two to three weeks before anything feels normal.

The Thanksgiving 10K on Nov 22 is 5 weeks out, which is on the edge. I would do it only if you treat it as a hard training run, not a race: start easy, finish strong, no all-out last mile. If you want to actually race a 10K, pick one in December or January and we will build to it properly.

If the quads stay sore past about 10 days, or anything sharp shows up when you start jogging again, stop and see a sports physio before pushing on.

new.analysis:
You executed the plan beautifully: every day done as written, and the race itself went out on pace through 20 before the quads gave up. That final 10K at 9:28/mi is textbook late-race fade from a slightly ambitious first-marathon-style pace plan, not a fitness problem. Twelve minutes off your previous time on a course with 617 ft of climb is a strong day.

The hard truth about marathon recovery is that the damage is deeper than it feels on Tuesday. The legs will feel fresh around day 4 or 5 and that is the moment to not run. Give the muscle fibres, tendons and immune system a full reset before loading them again, or you buy a nagging injury in November.

This week is mostly walking, with a short, slow jog only at the weekend if everything feels normal. Next week we lift it to short easy runs, no watch pressure, no structure. Then we talk about the goal that follows, because what we do in December depends entirely on what you want to chase. Have a think and tell me in your next check-in.
